target.title: fix(gateway): classify chat error kind via canonical failover reasons
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The chat UI's `errorKind` badge was classified by `detectErrorKind` in `src/infra/errors.ts` — a naive substring detector (`message.includes("429")`, `"rate limit"`, `"timeout"`, `"too many tokens"`) that independently re-derived the provider-failure fact the canonical failover stack already owns as a closed `FailoverReason` union. The two classifiers disagree today:

- A Groq TPM 413 ("too many tokens per minute") badge showed **`context_length`**, while failover classification correctly says **`rate_limit`** (its TPM hint explicitly rejects context overflow). Same error, opposite user-facing kinds.
- "quota exceeded" / "resource_exhausted" / CJK rate-limit strings, "fetch failed" / "socket hang up", and 429s present only on a nested `response.status` all classified as unknown in chat while failover classifies them correctly.

This is seam 5 (error → user-facing failure classification) of #104219, slice 1: delete the driftiest duplicate and migrate its single consumer to the canonical owner.

## Why This Change Was Made

`ErrorKind` + `detectErrorKind` are deleted from `src/infra/errors.ts` (also removing provider-taxonomy leakage from `infra/`). The only prod consumer, `src/gateway/server-chat.ts`, now maps `resolveFailoverReasonFromError` into the protocol's chat kind set (`rate_limit|overloaded → rate_limit`, `timeout|server_error → timeout`, `context_overflow → context_length`), with refusal kept as a chat-local check — refusal is a model stop-reason fact, not a `FailoverReason`, so the failover union is not widened. The chat kind type is now derived from the gateway-protocol `ChatEvent` schema type instead of a re-declared union; the protocol schema itself is unchanged, and the gateway→agents import direction already exists (`openai-compat-errors.ts`, `server-methods/agent.ts`).

Named follow-up slices (out of scope here, tracked on #104219): fold the private 429-status-walk/conversation-state/internal-error detectors in `provider-request-error-classifier.ts` into the canonical module; unify the duplicated timeout-code sets; remove `agent-runner-execution.ts`'s raw-message re-checks.

## User Impact

Chat/web-UI error badges become consistent with failover classification: TPM rate limits show `rate_limit` instead of `context_length`; quota, overload, CJK rate-limit, and network/socket failures show `rate_limit`/`timeout` instead of unknown. Conversely, bare "too many tokens"/"token limit" text without real overflow phrasing no longer over-matches to `context_length`. Diagnostics/UI only — no control-flow, retry, or delivery change. The ACP translator's `errorKind === "refusal"` → `stopReason` mapping is unaffected.

Note: the deleted names were transitively re-exported by the deprecated `openclaw/plugin-sdk/infra-runtime` star barrel; no in-repo or extension consumer exists, they were never on the preferred `error-runtime` surface, and `pnpm plugin-sdk:surface:check` passes.

## Evidence

- Drift sites: `src/infra/errors.ts:150-187` (deleted) vs canonical `src/agents/failover-error.ts` `resolveFailoverReasonFromError` + `src/agents/embedded-agent-helpers/failover-matches.ts` hint tables.
- Upstream trace: no prod producer sets lifecycle `data.errorKind` in the chat taxonomy today (`readChatErrorKind` remains a protocol-shaped validator), so the mapping is the sole classification path.
- Tests: table-driven mapping coverage in `src/gateway/server-chat.agent-events.test.ts` (12 cases: the Groq TPM 413 drift regression, quota/resource_exhausted, http 429, fetch failed/socket hang up/etimedout, context overflow, refusal strings, plain error → omitted); `detectErrorKind` unit tests deleted with the function, equivalent cases migrated.
- `git diff --numstat`: net prod **−5 LOC** (`infra/errors.ts` −39, `server-chat.ts` +34).
- Local: `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:test:src`, `pnpm check:import-cycles`, `pnpm plugin-sdk:surface:check`, focused vitest (282 tests), oxfmt — green.
- Remote (Blacksmith Testbox): `pnpm check:changed` exit 0. `pnpm test:changed` hit two known flaky groups under full shard load (`model-fallback.probe` async log-capture — same flake documented on #104319 — and `bash-tools.exec-runtime` suspension-timing tests, unrelated to this diff); all three suites pass isolated on the same lease (305/305).

Part of #104219 (seam 5: error classification, slice 1 of ~4).
